26 Cheap Streetwear Brands You Need in Your Closet | ClothedUp
26 Cheap Streetwear Brands You Need in Your Closet
Faith Lemaster
December 16, 2021
We may earn a commission from links on our website, but this doesn't influence the opinions of our editors. Last Updated: April 22, 2022
Looking for cheap streetwear brands? We’ve got you covered.
If you’re new to the streetwear game, it can be difficult to figure out where to start shopping, especially on a budget. With so many popular names thrown around, which streetwear brands truly live up to the hype? We’ve compiled a list of the top cheap streetwear brands to help you get started on your fashion journey!
If you’re simply looking to incorporate a few streetwear outfits for casual-dress days, or if you’re looking to overhaul your entire wardrobe, our list will help you find exactly what you’re looking for!
Cheap Streetwear Brands
📷 IG @stussy
Stüssy
If you have any prior knowledge of streetwear, Stüssy is probably the first brand that comes to mind. With their iconic logo and pop culture presence, they’ve built a large following in the streetwear world. So if you’re unsure of where to start, Stüssy is a solid first option!
Stüssy falls into the mid-tier price range, but considering how they’ve established themselves in the industry, it is a very reasonable price! If you’re all about brand logos and luxury fashion, Stüssy is the streetwear brand for you!
Shop Stussy
📷 IG @coopilito
Patta
Patta is one of the most popular streetwear brands today. They offer a large collection of tennis shoes—perfect for skateboarding and biking—as well as a fun collection of graphic tees !
While Patta is in the mid-tier price range, their attention to detail and quality craftsmanship make the pieces well worth it. If you’re looking for durable and trendy streetwear, Patta has exactly what you’re after!
Shop Patta
📷 IG @kith
KITH
Another iconic brand, KITH falls into the luxury arena of streetwear. A favorite among celebrities, KITH’s collections often combine softer elements such as floral prints and pastels as opposed to the louder colors and patterns often found in streetwear.
While KITH’s streetwear falls into the upper-tier price range, the quality of the product makes it well worth it. The fabric of their garments is effortlessly comfortable and durable while their shoes offer optimum support for walking, biking, and skateboarding. This is another great option for luxury fashion fans!
Shop KITH
📷 IG @charlie_birch
Palace
Palace is a one-stop shop for streetwear. Not only do they offer the standard shoes and graphic tees, but a wide array of accessories such as pins and hats as well!
Palace’s fleece garments are sure to keep you extra warm during those winter and fall months, so if you’re going for a morning walk or just stopping for a coffee before you get to work from your home office, you can be sure that you will be kept warm and stylish! Palace’s attention to detail is what makes them one of the top picks for our list.
Shop Palace
📷 IG @undercover_lab
Undercover
A truly luxury brand, Undercover offers high-end streetwear apparel. If you’re a fan of creative designers, Undercover is the perfect brand for you!
With their use of intricate Jacquard fabrics, structured jackets, and high-neck cuts, everything about this brand is luxurious in feel and style. So if you’re looking to maintain an air of high fashion while delving into the world of streetwear, Undercover has exactly what you’re after!
Shop Undercoverism
📷 IG @10deep
10.Deep
10.Deep is a brand full of loud, unique designs that will definitely grab attention.
Scott Sasso created this indie brand in 1995, drawing influences from music, art, and the rebellious culture of the 1990s.
Shop 10.Deep
📷 IG @jossanforsberg
HYPE.
HYPE. is another great streetwear brand for basics, but they also have other streetwear products such as a home section, and even a section for kids.
The brand started with a winning t-shirt desig n and soon grew into a worldwide streetwear company that sells something for everyone.
Shop HYPE.
📷 IG @commedesgarconsplay_th
Comme des Garçons Play
With one of the most iconic logos in the streetwear world, Comme des Garçons Play offers a wide variety of casual and comfortable garments perfect for day-to-day wear. With everything from a collaboration with Converse Chuck Taylor® to graphic tees and polos, there’s something for every outfit.
Comme des Garçons Play is perfect for the streetwear connoisseur who wants to style a put-together and classic look. Plus, the collection is available at Nordstrom, where you can find seasonal sales throughout the year!
Shop Nordstrom
📷 IG @youngcorey
The Hundreds
The Hundreds is one of the most affordable streetwear brands on our list! They offer a wide range of products, including tote bags and accessories in addition to apparel.
If you’re looking to stay on budget and just want to experiment with streetwear, this is a great place to start! They have standard logo pieces, which are traditional for streetwear, but they also have more creative pieces with abstract patterns, making this a great place for creatives to shop as well!
Shop The Hundreds
📷 IG @rico56k
Denim Tears
Denim Tears is one of the most unique brands on our list. While they offer an array of apparel, they also offer jewelry and even homeware !
They’re another creative brand on our list which branches out beyond the expected and ordinary. From the bright colors and patterns they use in their clothing to the artwork on their homeware, this brand truly thinks outside of the box.
Shop Denim Tears
📷 IG @davin_gentry
Diet Starts Monday
Pulling inspiration from past eras —the 70s-90s are most prominent—Diet Starts Monday provides the perfect vintage feel to the streetwear genre of fashion. So, if you’ve ever wished to sport the fashion of another decade, this is a great brand for you to check out!
Their apparel is easily recognizable with familiar, though abstract logos and icons, and their inspirations are apparent. So if you’re looking for the perfect throwback outfit that gives you the ability to stand out in a crowd, Diet Starts Monday is the place for you to shop!
Shop Diet Starts Monday
📷 IG @lewishamilton
A-Cold-Wall
A-Cold-Wall is another higher-end brand on our list. Drawing inspiration from seasonal designer collections, A-Cold-Wall is a luxury brand through and through. If you aren’t a fan of big logos, then this is an excellent option for you!
Focusing on minimalism-inspired patterns and logos, all of the pieces are classic and understated. It’s a very wearable collection that’s perfect for all tastes and occasions.
RELATED: 20 Luxury Sneaker Brands
Shop A-Cod-Wall
📷 IG @jodybreeze45
Obey
Another highly recognizable streetwear brand, Obey makes their way onto our list. Not only does their collection of apparel encapsulate aesthetic pieces of all of the other brands on our list, but they also happen to be one of the most affordable!
This is another great brand for streetwear beginners. If you’re looking to try out the streetwear look and determine your style preferences, Obey is a great place to start due to their wide range of pieces and affordable pricing!
Shop Obey
📷 IG @menacelosangeles
Menace
Menace is a Los Angeles-based brand with a small number of streetwear items online. They aren’t afraid to focus on darker, more controversial elements and have some great outerwear pieces.
Even though their selection is limited, you can sign up for their email subscription to be the first to know about any new collections dropping or popular items restocking.
Shop Menace
📷 IG @hufworldwide
HUF
If you’re looking for true skate streetwear, look no further than HUF. Founder Keith Hufnagel skateboarded as a kid, then became a professional skateboarder in 92 and officially opened HUF in 2002.
While it may not be the cheapest streetwear around, they do have some great t-shirts starting at $30.
Shop HUF
📷 IG @brwnstne.co
Brownstone

12 Canadian Streetwear Brands You Should Have on Your Radar
By Josh Walker for Complex Canada
Complex CA contributor who enjoys writing about culture.
Jul 07, 2020
COMMENT
Image via Atelier New Regime
Yes, the fashion industry has been ravaged by COVID-19, leaving countless people out of work and rendering previously planned strategies for 2020 redundant. Still, brands and designers in Canada have been adapting, moving ahead with dope drops to get us through these dark times, while demonstrating that fashion is also very much about community. Labels like Reigning Champ and Raised By Wolves, for instance, have been releasing special items in order to raise money for the Black Lives Matter movement and people afflicted by the pandemic.
Over the past decade, streetwear in Canada has turned into a movement of its own, bringing about brands inspired by the multiculturalism of Toronto as much as scenery deeper in the country. Here, we share some of the labels from that movement we’re stoked about, and think you should be too. These are 12 Canadian streetwear brands you should have on your radar.
Mr. Saturday
Image via Mr. Saturday
Mr. Saturday is the brainchild of Joey Gollish, a graduate of The Weeknd's creative incubator HXOUSE. The 26-year-old Torontonian is something of a fashion history buff, his work rife with tasteful nods to the nightlife and subcultures of days past. His Spring/Summer 2021 collection, for instance, mines New York City's party scene during the late '70s and early '80s, referencing iconic venues like Paradise Garage, The Ritz, and Danceteria. When the pandemic hit, Mr. Saturday released the SS20 Artist Relief Capsule, which raises money for the COVID-19 Response Fund, launched by HXOUSE and the Toronto Arts Council, supporting countless out-of-work creatives across Toronto. More recently, the brand also dropped its Priceless Lies T-shirt, 100 percent of its proceeds going to the NAACP and the Black Solidarity Fund. "There's a big focus on giving back to our community in what we do," Gollish tells us.
Get Fresh Company
Image via Get Fresh Company
Based out of Toronto, Get Fresh Company has always aimed to be more than just a clothing company. Part brand, part boutique, its beginnings date back to 2013 and, since then, it has always aimed to represent the youth of the city. They mill their own fabrics, create their own garments, and sell only 100 percent authentic drops. At present, they’ve got a collaboration set to release soon that’s been in the works for over a year.
Atelier New Regime
Image via Atelier New Regime
Though it started in 2009 as a passion project, Atelier New Regime has grown to become a staple of Montreal’s streetwear scene, where it has a flagship store on Notre-Dame St W decked out in orange (a colour synonymous with the brand). Atelier New Regime is founded on the principals of creativity, freedom, and self-expression. While the coronavirus pandemic has pushed the release of the brand’s next drop to July, the team has a homeware and jewelry collection in the works, as well as a debut denim and leather line. They will also be dropping a new collection at the end of the year temptingly named “The Birth of A New Regime."
4YE
Image via Publicist
Founded by wildly popular Toronto comedy duo Jae and Trey Richards, 4YE is a media company that's also emerging as a streetwear brand in its own right. Up to now, the brand's gained traction for its wavy durags, but lately it's been expanding its offerings to include classic hoodies and sweats. What's more, you can rock them with a clean conscience. Their "reWORK 1 of 1" collections source garments through Toronto's thrift market, which they remix via airbrushing and printed graphics. It's an effort to extend the lifecycle of second-hand clothing and combat the impact of fast-fashion. But most importantly, it looks dope as hell.
TheLegendsLeague
Image via TheLegendsLeague
Since it was founded by esteemed artist Bryan Espiritu, TheLegendsLeague has gone from strength to strength. After sharing his art online and gathering a loyal following, he transferred his talent to apparel. Today, that exists as an online space and brick-and-mortar store on Toronto’s Camden Street, stocking tees, headwear, hoodies, and more. As well as regularly announcing restocks of products, TheLegendsLeague has been throwing free, handmade masks into a selection of online orders. Their recently dropped "We're not alright but we'll be fine" tee could be the official shirt of 2020.
Carson Cartier
Image via Carson Cartier
Carson Cartier is a multi-disciplinary artist based out of Vancouver with an aim to bring together the worlds of painting, photography, digital art, and fashion. Part of that mission has been brought to life through various mens and womens collections. Within these, you might see denim jackets inspired by industrial workwear and the sounds of dark techno, or T-shirts characterized with industrial fabric spray paint. Recently, Cartier’s been working on a new collection, set to drop in fall, as well as new paintings and editorials.
Malice Studios
Image via Malice Studios
Led by a team of Montreal designers and Toronto rap artist 88 Camino of 88GLAM (who we recently spoke to about their surprise mixtape), Malice Studios is all about generating gear for the modern space cowboy/girl. “At the root of it, Malice is inspired by Japanese director Shinichir ō Watanabe’s Cowboy Bebop ,” Adamo Zinno, one of the brand’s co-founders, tells us. This month, Malice dropped their latest collection, Knocking On Heaven’s Door, via an online-only launch. It’s a collection that deals with their infatuation with death and what comes next, but with a positive twist; the items are printed with ‘Jesus is coming look busy’ and ‘knocking on heaven’s door.' The pieces themselves are produced locally, in downtown Montreal, and come from a place of authenticity. Even the name Malice is born from real experiences of being uncomfortable, and able to push personal boundaries.
Reigning Champ
Image via Reigning Champ
Reigning Champ has been delivering mens and womenswear drops from Vancouver since 2007. With a focus on quality, it’s a brand that lives to an ethos of "respect the details; master simplicity." As well as a performance line and other annual arrivals, Reigning Champ has embarked on a number of collaborations with brands like ASICS and New Era Cap. Their most recent collection is inspired by the timeless style and history of competitive rowing, bringing together lightweight staples and a full range of summer sweats.
Raised by Wolves
Image via Raised By Wolves
When Pete Williams decided to set up Raised by Wolves in 2008, he did so to put Canadian streetwear on the map. Since its inception, it’s safe to say he’s done exactly that. As well as embarking on collaborations with Timex, Timberland, and Reebok, the brand stocks tees, outerwear, footwear, and incense. Over the past month the brand’s been busy, launching a new collaboration with eyewear brand AKILA, as well as a Support Local program highlighting local businesses and artists they’ve worked with over the years. In the weeks to come they’re launching a digital cookbook with all sales being donated to the Ottawa Food Bank.
